prompted_for: Black-on-white equipment drawing for the CDMO industry page (ind-cdmo), source for art/ind-cdmo.png and the Illustration component

split into two suites by a central wall
one small process vessel per suite fed by an overhead pipe drop with valve
doors with windows on outer walls and between rooms, pass-through hatch on partition
layout_devices: repeated identical suites showing multi-client capacity
overhead pipe header running along each room to a drop
line_and_texture: no hatching, large empty floor areas
motifs: overhead PW header with point-of-use drop and valve
motion_implied: water travels along the overhead header into each suite in turn
valves open as the flow arrives

small process vessel on legs in each room
overhead pipe header with drop and valve
t2i_prompt: Clean isometric axonometric line drawing, black lines on a pure white background, thin uniform strokes, no shading, no fill, no text, no people. A roofless building block seen from above like a dollhouse cutaway, divided into identical rooms for <CONTENT>, double-line walls with modular panel seams, doors with small vision panels and a pass-through hatch. In each room one small piece of equipment fed by an overhead pipe header that drops down to a valve. Plenty of empty floor, generous white margin, suitable for tracing into a single-colour mask.
signature_idea: A CDMO as a roofless set of identical suites, each fed by the same overhead water header, showing one supply serving many clients.
strengths: calm and spacious, with lots of empty area
repeated suites communicate multi-product, multi-client work
pipe header shows Aquemi's water reaching the process
simple enough to stay legible at small sizes
weaknesses: equipment is tiny, so the water system itself barely registers
could read as any office or lab floor plan
pipe drops are small and easy to miss
brand_fit_why: Spare, precise axonometric lines and lots of space suit navy-on-limestone masks and the calm brand; the water story is understated.
